def solution(text: str) -> str:
    # From the examples:
    # '   ' -> '' (True)
    # 'hello world' -> 'helloworld' (True)
    # 'aba' -> 'aba' (True)
    # 'aA' -> 'aA' (True)
    # 'a' -> 'a' (True)
    # '12345' -> '12345' (True)
    #
    # False examples:
    # '123' -> '123_alt' (False)
    # 'a-b' -> 'a-b_alt' (False)
    # 'ab' -> 'ab_alt' (False)
    # 'hello' -> 'hello_alt' (False)
    # 'A' -> 'A_alt' (False)
    # '' -> '_alt' (False)
    # '09FwGcex3' -> '09FwGcex3_alt' (False)
    #
    # The pattern seems to be that the function removes all spaces from the input string.
    # For example, 'hello world' -> 'helloworld'
    # '   ' -> '' (all spaces removed)
    # Other strings without spaces remain unchanged.
    #
    # So the function returns the input string with all spaces removed.
    return text.replace(' ', '')
```
